n5.flagged_in_journal: usage_wrong #1 「入り口から外へ出てください。」 is perfectly acceptable, natural Japanese: exiting through the entrance is a real instruction actually used (e.g. when the exit is crowded or blocked), and 入り口 keeps its correct meaning. An acceptable use, so the item fails.

n4.flagged_in_journal: usage_wrong 3 (今度の若い人は元気がない) has a fully natural acceptable reading: 今度の＋person means 'the new/incoming person' (cf. 今度の先生, 今度来た人), so the sentence acceptably means 'the young person who just joined has no energy'. An acceptable use fails the item.

usage_wrong #3 「二十歳になったら親になる。」 is an ACCEPTABLE use of 親, not a clearly incorrect one. 親になる is a correct, extremely common collocation, and the sentence reads naturally as a life plan or prediction ("I'll become a parent when I turn 20") with no grammatical or collocational error. The intended trap (confusion with 大人になる) does not make the sentence wrong; a native speaker could produce it as-is. Replace with a sentence where 親 itself is misused (like the other two options 会社の親/アパートの親).

n3.flagged_in_journal: usage_wrong 1 '海外で泳いで、魚を見た' is fully acceptable Japanese — 海外で＋verb is standard ('I swam overseas (on a trip) and saw fish'); the intended 海外/海 confusion does not surface, so this is an acceptable use, not a misuse.

usage_wrong #1 「レポートの期間に間に合わない。」 is not clearly incorrect: 「(提出)期間に間に合う/間に合わない」 is an attested, natural pattern (出願期間に間に合わない, 募集期間に間に合わない), so with the routine ellipsis of 提出 the sentence has an acceptable reading ('won't make it within the report submission window'). The intended 期限-trap is ambiguous, and an acceptable use = FAIL.

usage_wrong 2 'ぬれた髪をアイロンで乾かした' is not clearly incorrect: アイロン standardly denotes a hair iron (ヘアアイロン) in hair contexts (髪をアイロンで伸ばす/巻く), and running one over damp hair is a real, nameable action, so a native can read this as an acceptable use. Secondary: paraphrase.correct プレス is weak — it names the pressing action, not the appliance, and 'ズボンにプレスをかけてもらう' is marginal Japanese.

paraphrase.correct ボールペン is not a synonym/paraphrase of インク — it is a tool, インク is the substance; 'インクで書く' equally covers 万年筆 and gel pens, so 'ボールペンで書かなくてはならないか' does not preserve the meaning. Metonymic association, not a paraphrase.

usage_wrong #1 「二人の係はとてもいい。」 is not clearly wrong: [numeral]+の+係 is standard grammar, so it reads acceptably as 'the two attendants are very nice' or 'the clerk assigned to the two is very good' (bare 係 for a staff member is normal, e.g. 係に聞いてください). The intended 関係-trap reading is not the only one, so an acceptable use exists = FAIL. Additionally #3 「旅行の係が高くついた」 collides with the real homophone 掛かり(かかり)=expenses, where 「旅行のかかりが高くついた」 is legitimate Japanese; only the kanji choice keeps it wrong, making it weak in aural/kana presentation.

usage_wrong sentences are ACCEPTABLE uses of 今回: 「彼は今回、とても忙しい。」 is perfectly natural Japanese meaning 'this time around / on this occasion he is very busy' (e.g. 前回は暇だったが、今回はとても忙しい), and 「今回は何時ですか。」 is acceptable when asking what time this instance of a recurring event takes place (今回は何時からですか). At least two of the three sentences have natural correct readings, so they fail the requirement of being clearly incorrect uses.

paraphrase.correct 完璧 is not a real synonym of 完成: 完成 = completion/being finished (≈できあがり・完了), 完璧 = perfection/flawlessness — a distinction JLPT itself tests. The equivalence only seems to work because the example 「練習が完成を生む。」 is an unnatural calque of 'practice makes perfect'; teaching 完成=完璧 mis-trains learners. A native editor would reject this pairing.
